label: late original-phase positions (t=5-7), content-dependent
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase (99% of mass), at absolute positions t=4-8 and peaking at t=6, usually in the last 1-3 inputs before <DEL> in sequences with L>=7. It is weak at the delimiter (0.8% of mass) and never fires at t<=2 or in the copy phase. The position window alone recovers about 92% of mass but only about 5% precision, so most late original steps stay silent. Which ones fire depends on content in a way no simple predicate captures. Rates are higher when the input is 2/l/f/g, when the previous input is a/l/d/i, and when the prefix holds tokens like x, f, n, w, l, z or h (the first token is often 2 or l). The largest activations (about 3.0) occur on input 2 right after a or l. A combined token-plus-prefix clause reached only F1 0.28 on dev, so the content dependence is distributed and has not been explained.
